name: Pepe the Frog
blurb: A green cartoon frog from Matt Furie's 2005 comic Boy's Club, used as a reaction face
title: Pepe the Frog Meme: Meaning, Origin & History
description: Pepe the Frog is a cartoon frog from Matt Furie's 2005 comic Boy's Club. His line "feels good man" spread on 4chan in 2008 and he became a reaction image.
h1: What is the Pepe the Frog meme?
answer: Pepe the Frog is a green, wide-eyed cartoon frog drawn by the American artist Matt Furie for his comic Boy's Club, which he started posting on Myspace in 2005. A panel of Pepe saying "feels good man" was posted to 4chan in 2008, and the frog turned into one of the internet's most-used reaction images: sad Pepe, smug Pepe, crying Pepe and countless edits. Today he is best known as a family of chat emotes and reaction faces.

body: Pepe is a simple green frog with a round face, big droopy eyes and wide red-brown lips. In the original comic he is a laid-back slacker who lives with three roommates. The meme versions keep the face but change the mood: a teary sad frog, a smug half-smile, a sweaty nervous look, or a tiny grin with the words "feels good man".
Because the face is so expressive and easy to redraw, people use Pepe the way others use emoji: to show a feeling quickly.

head: Date
Event
rows: Matt Furie posts Boy's Club on Myspace; Pepe is one of its four characters.
A scan of the "feels good man" page is posted to 4chan's /b/ board and spreads as a reaction image.
The "feels bad man" sad frog version starts circulating.
Pepe is widely called one of the biggest memes of the year; collections of "rare Pepes" become a joke of their own.
The Anti-Defamation League adds Pepe to its hate-symbol database after extremist misuse; in October Furie launches #SavePepe with the ADL.
Furie publishes a comic showing Pepe's funeral, widely reported as him "killing off" the character.
The documentary Feels Good Man, about Furie and Pepe, premieres at the Sundance Film Festival.

body: Most people never read Boy's Club: the meme took one panel, where Pepe explains why he pulls his pants all the way down to pee, and turned his catchphrase into a general "this feels great" reaction.

ul: Reaction images: sad Pepe after losing, smug Pepe after winning an argument.
"Feels good man" / "feels bad man": short captions for a good or bad moment.
Chat emotes on streaming sites, added through third-party extensions: monkaS (nervous, sweating), PepeHands (crying), PepeLaugh, FeelsBadMan.
"Rare Pepe": a running joke that some unusual Pepe edits are collectible.

body: Pepe is a classic. In 2016 some extremist groups used the frog, and the ADL listed those specific uses as a hate symbol, while noting that most Pepe images are not. Furie has said many times that he disagrees with that misuse; he campaigned to reclaim the character, symbolically buried him in 2017, and has taken legal action over unauthorized uses of Pepe, including a 2019 copyright settlement.
In everyday chats and streams, Pepe is used as an ordinary reaction face, mostly with no political meaning at all. The character and its copyright belong to Matt Furie.

faq.a: The American artist Matt Furie, who drew him for his comic Boy's Club starting in 2005.
It is Pepe's catchphrase from the original comic. Online it is a caption for a moment that feels satisfying; "feels bad man" is the sad version.
Not in general. The ADL lists only Pepe images used in a hateful context. Most Pepe memes and emotes are everyday reactions, and Furie has rejected the extremist uses.
